  Code of Ethics

As City of Irwindale Parks & Recreation Commissioners, our fundamental duty is to serve the public good. We are
committed to the principle of an efficient and professional local government. We will be exemplary in obeying the letter
and spirit of Local, State and Federal laws and City policies affecting the operation of the government and in our private
life. We will be independent and impartial in our judgment and actions.

We will work for the common good of the City of Irwindale community and not for any private or personal interest. We
will endeavor to treat all people with respect and civility. We will commit to observe the highest standards of morality
and integrity, and to faithfully discharge the duties of our office regardless of personal consideration. We shall refrain
from abusive conduct, personal charges or verbal attacks upon the character or motives of others.

We will inform ourselves on public issues, listen attentively to public discussions before the body, and focus on the
business at hand. We will base our decisions on the merit and substance of that business. We will be fair and equitable
in all actions, claims or transactions. We shall not use our official position to influence government decisions in which
we have a financial interest or where we have a personal relationship that could present a conflict of interest, or create
a perception of a conflict of interest.

We shall not take advantage of services or opportunities for personal gain by virtue of our public office that are not
available to the public in general. We shall refrain from accepting gifts, favors or promises of future benefit that might
compromise our independence of judgment or action or give the appearance of being compromised.

We will behave in a manner that does not bring discredit or embarrassment to the City of Irwindale. We will be honest
in thought and deed in both our personal and official lives.

Ultimate responsibility for complying with this Code of Ethics rests with the individual elected official. In addition to any
other penalty as provided by law, violation of this Code of Ethics may be used as a basis for disciplinary action or censure
of a Commissioner.

These things we hereby pledge to do in the interest and purposes for which our government has been established.

  SPONTANEOUS COMMUNICATIONS
This is the time set aside for members of the audience to speak on items not on this agenda. State law prohibits any
Commission discussion or action on such communications unless 1) the Commission by majority vote finds that a
catastrophe or emergency exists; or 2) the Commission by at least four votes finds that the matter (and need for action
thereon) arose within the last five days. Since the Commission cannot (except as stated) participate, it is requested that
all such communications be made in writing so as to be included on the next agenda for full discussion and action. If a
member of the audience feels he or she must proceed tonight, then each speaker will be limited to 3 minutes unless
such time limits are extended.

5050 N. IRWINDALE AVENUE  WEDNESDAY

The Irwindale PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION met in regular session at the above time
and place.

  Vice Chair Belen Zepeda (arrived at 6:01 p.m.); Chair Paula Fraijo

  Absent: Commissioner Marguerite Sapien

  Also present: Elizabeth Rodriguez, Public Services Director; Priscilla
  Zepeda, Recreation Manager; Daniel Grijalva, Aquatics Supervisor,
  Jeff Wagner, IT Manager; and Armando Hegdahl, Management
  Analyst

COMMUNICATIONS  There were no speakers.

ITEM NO. 1A  MINUTES
MINUTES

END OF CONSENT CALENDAR

RECREATION
MANAGER UPDATE

RECREATION  Recreation Manager Zepeda provided an update on the following
MANAGER ZEPEDA  programs and activities:

  1) Staff is looking into the costs associated with implementing Spin
  Classes and/or machines and will present these items in the
  department’s budget requests for the Fiscal Year 23/24 budget.
  2) Staff has also mailed out an informational flyer regarding the
  upcoming Dog Obedience class, which begins on October 13.
  3) Staff is also drafting a Dismissal Policy, which will be presented
  to the Commission at its November meeting for input.
 PARKS & RECREATION COMMISSION MINUTES  OCTOBER 5, 2022
REGULAR MEETING  PAGE 2

  4) The commission previously asked about splitting the Teeny Tots
  class to two classes. Staff has reached out to the families of
  participants, but only one participant has so far indicated a slight
  interest. Staff will continue monitoring attendance levels and will
  report to the commission in the future.
  5) Fall classes, such as Karate, Baby Ballet, Yoga AM, Flag
  Football, Cornhole League, and others, have begun.
  6) Staff is working with the Dog Obedience class instructor to
  inquire about adding a second class, since there are currently
  seven individuals signed up on the interest list.
  7) The Kindness Krew is working on a Household Items Donations
  Drive, with donated items to be donated to the YWCA Women
  and Children’s Center. Flyers will be mailed out to residents
  soon.
  8) The following trips have been scheduled:
  A) Teeny Tots – Pumpkin Patch – October 10
  B) Tiny Tots – Pumpkin Patch – October 18
  C) Teen Trip – Universal Studios Halloween Haunt – October 15
  D) Family Trip – Descanso Gardens – October 14
  E) Family Trip – San Clemente Outlets – November 19
  F) Fall Day Camp Trip – Universal Studios – November 22
  9) The MariachiFest special events concluded last Friday. Staff will
  place an item on next month’s meeting to discuss possibly
  changing the events to Thursdays in 2023.
  10) The following events are scheduled to take place next month:
  A) Veterans Ceremony – November 11
  B) Scarecrow Alley – November 21
  11) The City Council is set to declare October as Anti-Bullying
  Month. The KidZone and Tiny & Teeny Tots are working on
  projects and activities focused on being kind to others.
  12) Numerous Halloween-themed events have been scheduled. Staff
  is also seeking donations for the Halloween Spooktacular Bingo
  and volunteers for games.
  13) Several photographs from resident Jenna Soria are currently
  displayed at the Recreation Center.
  14) The Dan Diaz Recreation Center will serve as a polling place for
  the November elections, from November 5 – 8.
  15) Customer Service Week is this week. Manager Zepeda
  recognized the many staff members from various departments
  that help the city programs and events function.
  16) Lissette Rodriguez was announced as the Recreation
  Department’s Employee of the Quarter.
  17) She also discussed her role in the CA Parks and Recreation
  Department’s JEDI Challenge.

CHAIR FRAIJO  Chair Fraijo suggested that the flyers that will be mailed out include
  Halloween safety information.

VICE CHAIR ZEPEDA  Vice Chair Zepeda suggested that Police Officers visit the children in
  their classes to offer safety tips.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Roman suggested displaying safety tips on the city’s
ROMAN  electronic marquee. She also suggested cutting trips that typically
  see fewer attendees to add more seats for holiday family trips, and
  requested to be updated on the JEDI Challenge.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Ortiz commended Recreation Supervisors Marez and
ORTIZ  Osterheim for the professionalism they exhibited when dealing with
  an irate customer.

AQUATICS
SUPERVISOR UPDATE

SUPERVISOR GRIJALVA Supervisor Grijalva provided an update on the following programs
  and activities:

  1) The summer season classes wrapped up last month, with the
  last day of recreational swimming being held on Sunday,
  September 25.
  2) The extended recreational swimming held on weekends
  averaged about 80+ participants.
  3) The Swim Team has a total of 30 swimmers, and will compete
  against Duarte’s Swim Team on October 22.
  4) The Swim Team will enjoy a Halloween-inspired “Monster Splash
  Bash” toward the end of the month.
  5) The fall sessions of Aqua-fitness, Lap Swim, Senior Splash,
  Aqua Walk, and Aqua Stand Up are underway.
  6) He also reported that he attended the Southern California Public
  Pool Operators Association meeting on September 8 in West
  Hollywood, and will attend these meetings every month.
  7) He and three Assistant Pool Managers will attend the 52 nd
  Annual SCMAF Institute conference in Carson beginning
  tomorrow.
  8) He will also attend the California Aquatic Management School in
  Lake Arrowhead from October 19-21.

CHAIR FRAIJO  Chair Fraijo commended Supervisor Grijalva for ensuring continuous
  education for himself and his staff.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Roman requested that Supervisor Grijalva work on
ROMAN  implementing an Aquatics Store next year.

PUBLIC WORKS
SUPERVISOR UPDATE  Director Rodriguez presented the following update:

  1) Uneven pavers at Jardin de Roca Park have mostly been repaired.
  2) Staff has also retrofitted all the light poles to LED lights at El Nido
  Park. Lighting at Irwindale Park will also be replaced with LED
  bulbs.
  3) The park restrooms will have toilet seat cover dispensers installed
  at the end of the week.
  4) The lighting at the gym floor will be repaired next week.
  5) Staff is preparing for upcoming events, including the Halloween
  Spooktacular and the Christmas Spectacular and Mayor’s Tree
  Lighting Ceremony.
  6) She thanked staff for filling in for others that were temporarily
  unable to work.

CHAIR FRAIJO  Chair Fraijo noted the hard work of the Yard staff in addressing all the
  Commissioners’ concerns when they conducted the park walk-
  through in March. She also thanked the Irwindale Community
  Foundation for financially supporting many city events.

COMMISSIONER  Commissioner Ortiz requested that the palm fronds near the softball
ORTIZ  and gazebo areas be trimmed, to which Director Rodriguez
  responded by advising that the trimming is scheduled to be conducted
  within the next couple of weeks.

PUBLIC SERVICES
DIRECTOR UPDATE  Director Rodriguez presented the following update:

  1) She thanked the Managers, Supervisors, and staff of the
  Recreation, Aquatics, and Public Works Departments for their
  tireless work during the hot summer months.
  2) Staff continues working with the grant contractors to further efforts
  in securing grants that would help offset the costs of projects and
  programs.
  3) Staff is awaiting a few changes to the plan for the Irwindale Park
  Improvement Project before sending the project out to bid. An
  update will be presented in November.

COMMISSIONER ITEMS
AND REQUESTS

VICE CHAIR ZEPEDA  Vice Chair Zepeda asked why the MariachiFest events would be
  rescheduled to Thursdays instead of Fridays, to which Manager
  Zepeda advised that the thought was to avoid having the event
  compete with Friday Night Lights, and noted that the subject will be
  discussed at the November meeting.
